stem.en: Assertion (A): The zygote formed after fertilisation immediately attaches to the uterus wall. Reason (R): The uterus wall is always prepared to receive the zygote. Choose the correct option.

text.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

feedback.en: The zygote first travels and divides, so A is false.

text.en: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

feedback.en: A is false, because the zygote forms in the oviduct and takes time to reach the uterus.

text.en: A is true, but R is false.

feedback.en: R is indeed false, but A is false too, because the zygote first travels along the oviduct.

text.en: A is false, but R is true.

feedback.en: A is false, but so is R: the lining thickens and is shed in a monthly cycle.

text.en: Both A and R are false.

feedback.en: Correct. The zygote travels and divides first, and the lining is ready only at part of the cycle.

explanation.en: The zygote forms in the oviduct, then divides by mitosis as it travels to the uterus, so it does not attach at once. The lining is not always prepared either: it thickens during the cycle and is shed if no egg is fertilised.

hints.en: Is the lining the same on every day of the month?
